reviewer.basis: A separate hostile review pass challenged the completed v5 documentation model, generated migration, mechanical checks, package lifecycle, and both retained development legs. It was performed in the same Codex session as authorship, so this records cognitive role separation rather than personal or organizational independence.

questions.challenge: Can a declared boundary conceal an unowned volatile decision, reverse policy dependencies, or make a component depend on a counterpart identity?
questions.conclusion: The canonical architecture names local roles, decisions, change scenarios, contracts, interactions, and technology owners; distinct structural checks and mutations cover ownership and direction, while semantic adequacy remains review judgment.

questions.challenge: Can structural protocol conformance pass while behavioral terms, implementation variants, or test-term traceability are absent?
questions.conclusion: The contract-conformance model joins every local contract to representations, behavioral terms, implementation capabilities, suites, and exact test evidence; the checker rejects missing and orphaned terms without claiming those oracles are sufficient.

questions.challenge: Which expected, exceptional, subprocess, generated-artifact, or persistence failure can escape without a typed outcome, causal diagnostic, or recovery owner?
questions.conclusion: The operational model connects active capabilities to translation, recovery, correlated terminal outcomes, and executable evidence. Dual-platform adopter runs exercised the same obligations and exposed platform-specific launch, listener-teardown, selector, model, and typing defects before release acceptance.

questions.challenge: Can accepted work, a launched process, cleanup, a generated projection, or the learning store consume unbounded local time or resources without an owned stop path?
questions.conclusion: All activated capability obligations resolve to explicit lifecycle phases, limits, recovery records, and tests. These records decide repository-local ownership only and do not claim whole-application liveness.

questions.challenge: Can untrusted project input or retained learning data gain stronger local trust, reach an unauthorized sink, or survive beyond its stated policy?
questions.conclusion: Every declared contract is joined to one trust boundary and every intentionally handled class records local roles, sinks, retention, redaction, and evidence. The model deliberately stops at this repository boundary.

questions.challenge: Can a non-exception refusal, timeout, degraded condition, or failed gate disappear behind process status without correlation and cause-preserving diagnostics?
questions.conclusion: The operational outcomes and diagnostic laws require stable identities, correlation, terminal observability, and preserved causes; tests exercise gate refusal and timeout as data. Semantic usefulness of emitted context remains reviewable.

questions.challenge: Can generated doctrine views, mirrored host skills, development images, vendored manifests, or a delivered archive drift from authored source while the gate stays green?
questions.conclusion: Generated drift and byte-identical host mirrors are checked, vendoring preserves a manifest, and every Linux invocation reconciles current build inputs. The Docker frontend and base are digest-pinned, the context admits only three declared inputs, and the checkout enters through a non-root managed-volume projection. Two independently staged 271-member archives are byte-identical, both shipped legs passed all eleven source-gate stages, and archive construction refuses absent or floating direct Python verifier dependencies.

questions.challenge: Can a mechanism be counted as enforcement without a mutation proving that its stated observable proposition is rejected?
questions.conclusion: The evidence registry separates direct, proxy, behavioral, tool, and review claims; review-only obligations do not enter the mutation census. Both release legs report D=180 above its 167 floor, all 194 declared mutations provoking their rule, and S=192 with no undiscriminated exact strategy or rule identity. Validation refuses rule-only or pending credit and generated proposition boilerplate; the mutation adapter also refuses zero work, survivors, and non-verdict tool outcomes.

questions.challenge: Which v5 entity contract or semantic-step comment can disagree with the exact implementation and tests it now describes?
questions.conclusion: The hostile pass found that mechanically conforming generated templates had survived the initial migration as thousands of semantically empty comments. The affected source was rewritten by ownership family, known template families and the generic callable-effects clause now fail DOC-019 or DOC-027, and L-0116 retains the failure mode. These closed-shape checks are not treated as proof that all remaining prose is true.

questions.challenge: Which fact is duplicated across a Doxygen contract and ordinary narration, or attached below the highest layer able to express it correctly?
questions.conclusion: The review samples entity, local-binding, branch, transformation, state, and effect documentation against the exclusive two-layer allocation and records any residual ambiguity as a defect.

questions.challenge: Which narration preserves an earlier mechanism, workaround, ordering, or state sequence that current code no longer executes?
questions.conclusion: Content-bound scope freshness invalidates this acceptance after any governed file changes; the hostile pass additionally searches current comments for historical or contradicted mechanics.

questions.challenge: Which identifier hides a relevant semantic dimension, violates broad-to-specific ordering, or uses an abbreviation with an undeclared or competing meaning?
questions.conclusion: The repository model declares its actual scopes and controlled vocabulary; lexical checks decide internal consistency while this review retains the domain-semantic residual.

objections.statement: The author and adversarial reviewer labels represent two passes by the same Codex session, so the structure cannot establish personal or organizational independence.
objections.resolution: The artifact states the limitation without claiming independent identity. Native Windows and independent Linux execution provide platform separation and field evidence, but are not misrepresented as cognitive independence.
objections.review_trigger: Repeat with a genuinely independent reviewer when one is available or whenever the independence claim changes.

objections.statement: Raw worktree hashing gave identical Git text different review identities under Windows CRLF and Linux LF checkout projection.
objections.resolution: Canonicalize CRLF to LF only for valid UTF-8 inputs, retain invalid UTF-8 bytes exactly, and exercise both checkout projections in a proof-of-failure test.
objections.review_trigger: Review again if scope serialization, supported platforms, text encoding, or digest algorithms change.

objections.statement: Import-linter writes a replaceable cache inside the governed tree, and including it made a verifier run invalidate the semantic content it had just checked.
objections.resolution: Add the named import-linter cache to the fixed environment exclusions and prove that creating it after review leaves the governed identity unchanged.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever a supported verifier introduces a new repository-local cache or an exclusion name changes.

objections.statement: Ten binding rules named AST or markdown checks whose own rules tuples and module documentation stated that those mechanisms could never emit the named rule IDs.
objections.resolution: Route semantic translation, mutation, transition-ordering, channel-seam, concept, immutability, and prior coordinator judgments to content-bound structured review; retain syntax checks only for the narrower predicates they actually report, and exclude review-only rules from the mechanical discrimination census.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever a semantic-only rule acquires a syntax mechanism or the discrimination census changes its definition of a mechanical claim.

objections.statement: A missing doc_engine field was converted to none, silently deactivating Doxygen-specific rules, while DOC-014 claimed the field was mandatory; DOC-008 also emitted real findings without listing its own rule ID.
objections.resolution: Require the sole Doxygen engine explicitly in every v5 declaration, reject an unmigrated v4 declaration with an actionable diagnostic, retain an emitting fallback only for direct legacy checks, and witness the failures in the discrimination matrix.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever declaration defaults, documentation engines, doc_style predicates, or aggregate-gate configuration loading changes.

objections.statement: An aggregate runner could invoke Ruff, mypy, pyright, or pytest without proving which project configuration or targets the tool consumed; several of those tools can exit zero after examining nothing.
objections.resolution: Bind each adapter to the exact root pyproject digest and consumed fields, pass configuration and repository-local targets explicitly, count non-empty subjects before launch, require pyright and pytest to corroborate actual execution, and record the observed distribution version and argv.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever a tool changes configuration discovery, target semantics, report format, module entry point, or supported platform.

objections.statement: The import-contract wrapper hard-coded src even though v4 declarations admit explicit source roots, so a nonstandard layout could be checked against no package or an unintended importable package.
objections.resolution: Pass every declared import root explicitly, place only resolved repository-local roots on sys.path, refuse parent or sibling escape before import-linter starts, and retain the legacy src default only for direct wrapper compatibility.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever source-root declaration, editable installation, namespace package discovery, or import-linter graph construction changes.

objections.statement: A documentation subprocess can exit zero after its configured inputs are filtered out, while an absent or implicitly narrowed engine can suppress the subprocess entirely.
objections.resolution: Require Doxygen as the explicit sole engine, bind INPUT to the exact declared source roots, enforce warning-as-error and offline posture, run into ephemeral output, and count generated pages plus relationship families before accepting process status.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever an engine, input grammar, output generator, warning policy, or documentation source-root convention changes.

objections.statement: Source-tree tests can remain green while wheel membership, source-distribution metadata, runtime dependencies, entry points, or clean installation are broken; PYTHONPATH substitution conceals that entire defect class.
objections.resolution: Build wheel and sdist from an ephemeral copy that excludes VCS, agent, cache, and prior build state; require exact build-backend pins; inspect Name and Version inside both archives; install the wheel into a fresh venv; and run metadata, import, and declared entry-point probes under isolated Python without the source tree on sys.path.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever build isolation, archive metadata, dependency installation, entry-point declaration, venv behavior, or artifact probe configuration changes.

objections.statement: Cosmic Ray 8.7.0 treats an unlaunchable test command as an incompetent outcome, but its baseline exits green and its survival-rate calculation counts that outcome as a killed mutant; a quoting or environment defect can therefore manufacture a perfect score.
objections.resolution: Generate a shlex-safe command with portable path spellings, dump both baseline and mutation sessions independently, require a normal surviving baseline, require every generated mutant to complete normally as killed or survived, and reject every incompetent, abnormal, pending, empty, or surviving result before consulting the score tool.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever Cosmic Ray's command parser, baseline semantics, work-result schema, survival calculation, or Windows process behavior changes.

objections.statement: The delivered requirements file once carried only YAML and JSON-schema support even though the canonical adopter gate invokes Ruff, mypy, pyright, import-linter, three pytest controls, build, and mutation. A fresh package could therefore be structurally installed while most required verification was unavailable.
objections.resolution: Ship exact pins for every Python gate branch, make archive construction reject absent or non-exact pins, and retain Doxygen plus Graphviz as execution-checked native prerequisites in both development legs. V5 removes the alternate Sphinx branch instead of carrying an optional verifier path.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever a gate adapter, supported documentation engine, Python floor, distribution name, or verifier version changes.

objections.statement: A zero mechanism gap and a synthetic package lifecycle do not certify v5 until the discipline source, application and single-component package shapes, documentation projection, and release archive pass on both supported legs.
objections.resolution: Run all eleven source-gate stages through Windows/Conda and Linux/Docker, round-trip both in-scope repository shapes through the staged package, require real Doxygen relationships, and compare independently staged archives byte-for-byte. The authorized python-doctrine-test exercise remains field observation of fail-closed authorship debt, not a claim that v5 made that adopter conformant.
objections.review_trigger: Repeat both platform gates, package-shape round trips, and archive construction whenever shipped package inputs change.

objections.statement: Code and annotations that pass on the authoring platform can name subprocess flags, control signals, socket teardown behavior, or readiness assumptions absent or different on the other supported platform.
objections.resolution: Run both strict checkers, tests, mutation, build, and clean-install probes natively on Windows and Linux. Replace platform-stub-dependent constants with typed numeric protocol values, bound listener teardown, and make selector evidence wait for the first productive readiness turn.
objections.review_trigger: Review again when supported platforms, Python/typeshed versions, process control, sockets, selectors, or lifecycle behavior change.

objections.statement: An ignored legacy release archive at an adopter root entered content-bound review scope on the source worktree but was absent from a clean clone, so identical authored commits received different review identities.
objections.resolution: Preserve the legacy archive byte-for-byte under the excluded build area, record its digest and disposition, and regenerate the adopter review over the authored repository scope shared by source and clean clone.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever ignored delivery artifacts, fixed environment exclusions, or clean-clone scope semantics change.

objections.statement: A repository can carry duplicated canonical-model records or omit strict Pyright configuration while narrower tests and the first type checker remain green.
objections.resolution: Require one envelope per declared budget class, reject missing and duplicate canonical records, bind strict Pyright to the declared source tree, and certify both checkers and all model checks on both platforms.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever model schemas, uniqueness joins, type-checker configuration, or declared analysis targets change.

objections.statement: The v5 meta-test retained a 420-second child ceiling after the rejection census expanded to 194 cases; the canonical Windows release suite exceeded that inherited budget after the same census had passed as a standalone gate.
objections.resolution: Preserve every rejection case and raise the finite child ceiling to 540 seconds inside a distinct 600-second pytest ceiling. The exact nested proof then passed in the non-skipped Windows release command and in the unchanged Linux gate.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever the discrimination census, process-launch strategy, supported Windows environment, or gate-entry timeout policy changes.

objections.statement: A floating Dockerfile frontend or base tag can change executable bytes without a repository diff, while a broad build context can send source history, credentials, or application code to a remote builder even when no later COPY retains it.
objections.resolution: Pin both frontend and multi-platform Miniforge base by sha256 digest, exclude the complete context first, re-admit only the environment declaration, dependency-free checker, Dockerfile, and entry point, and test that exact allowlist.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever a remote image, Dockerfile frontend, build-context member, secret mount, or build service changes.

objections.statement: The Python Pyright launcher silently provisions Node through nodeenv when the declared Node executable is not visible, adding a network action and a second unverified runtime to an apparently locked gate.
objections.resolution: Pin Node in the shared Conda declaration, execution-check it, put the declared environment first on PATH before Pyright starts, disable the alternative Node wheel strategy, and require a successful image-build Pyright probe. The first hostile build exposed the fallback and the corrected build ran Pyright 1.1.407 through Node 22.21.1 without nodeenv provisioning.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever Pyright's Python wrapper, Node resolution strategy, PATH construction, or pinned runtime changes.

objections.statement: Accepting a pre-existing local v4.1.0 image tag as proof of content could run an image built from earlier or dirty inputs against the current repository.
objections.resolution: Route every Linux invocation through the digest-pinned Docker build. Content-addressed cached layers keep unchanged runs bounded while Docker re-evaluates the current lock, checker, entry point, context policy, and Dockerfile before retagging.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever image naming, cache use, build invocation, or build-input membership changes.

objections.statement: Docker Desktop may expose a discoverable but deliberately nonfunctional docker command inside a WSL distribution with integration disabled, causing the Linux leg to fail before trying the working Windows Docker CLI.
objections.resolution: Accept a discovered Linux docker command only after its engine answers docker version; otherwise select Docker Desktop's Windows executable and convert the context and mount through wslpath. The actual host topology exercised this fallback successfully.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever Docker Desktop's WSL integration, executable locations, engine probe, or path conversion changes.

objections.statement: Windows PowerShell 5.1 promotes native stderr from conda.bat to ErrorRecord; under a global stop policy, the expected absent-environment probe terminated before the launcher could enter its create-or-repair path.
objections.resolution: Temporarily use non-terminating native stderr semantics only around each Conda process, capture LASTEXITCODE before restoring the strict policy, and make that status the sole success decision. A freshly packaged launcher then created, verified, used, and removed an isolated environment.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever the supported PowerShell version, Conda entry point, native error policy, or process invocation changes.

objections.statement: Running the container as root can leave root-owned build products on the bind mount, while a wrapper that does not exec the requested tool can absorb stop signals and orphan verifier subprocesses.
objections.resolution: Run with the invoking numeric uid/gid, create disposable writable home and XDG directories for identities absent from passwd, trust only /workspace for Git ownership, use Docker init, prohibit privileged mode, and exec the requested command. A mounted run observed uid 1000 and direct tool execution.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever mount ownership, user namespaces, entry-point behavior, init handling, or stop semantics change.

objections.statement: The initial source-wide v5 migration satisfied association and vocabulary checks while retaining thousands of repeated comments that merely renamed syntax or narrated generic checker mechanics; a green lexical gate therefore overstated semantic completion.
objections.resolution: Audit repeated prose across the complete governed source, rewrite confirmed families by their actual owner and invariant, reject the closed generated families plus the generic callable-effects clause, and retain L-0116 so later mass migrations repeat the content census before qualification. The residual for novel plausible-but-empty prose remains human review.
objections.review_trigger: Repeat the repetition census after any mass documentation migration, classifier broadening, or generated prose transformation.

objections.statement: The LEARN-006 behavioral mutation included two generated comments in its replacement preimage, so making those comments truthful caused the rejection table to drift without changing the behavior the mutation was meant to damage.
objections.resolution: Anchor the mutation only on the two executable sync statements and add a regression assertion that its preimage contains no narration. Both platform censuses then observed LEARN-006 and all other declared mutations provoke their exact rules.
objections.review_trigger: Review again whenever a repository-based mutation uses comments, documentation strings, generated prose, or other non-behavioral text as its preimage.

objections.statement: Windows packages default to the shared Conda environment name claude. Two already-running legacy launchers rewrote that prefix to an older exact lock after v5 preflight, making an otherwise conformant discrimination control fail until v5 repaired the environment again.
objections.resolution: Retain fail-closed execution checking before every v5 command and record the observed legacy transactions and repairs. Qualification ran both final legs without a concurrent legacy writer, but v5 does not claim it can prevent an older launcher that does not participate in a shared lock protocol from mutating the same named prefix mid-command.
objections.review_trigger: Replace this acceptance with a versioned environment identity or cross-version command-lifetime lock, or review whenever the default environment name and launcher concurrency model change.

objections.statement: The shared environment pins direct versions but does not hash Conda packages, wheels, or transitive Python resolutions; a repository diff therefore cannot alone prove the exact downloaded artifact bytes.
objections.resolution: State the limitation in the executable declaration and release notes, execution-check every native tool and direct Python distribution, pin both remote container roots by digest, and keep byte-exact reproducibility claims confined to the discipline archive. A hash-locked cross-platform wheelhouse remains future supply-chain work.
objections.review_trigger: Replace this acceptance when Conda explicit locks and hash-checked Python artifacts exist for both supported legs, or review whenever channels and dependency resolution change.

conclusion: The v5 documentation discipline and combined Claude Code/Codex package are acceptable for release. The final hostile pass rejected the initial mechanically conforming comment ceremony, the repaired 180-file source is clean under all four documentation checks, both development legs passed the same eleven-stage gate, and independently staged archives are byte-identical. No unresolved blocker remains; the two high or medium operational limitations are explicitly accepted rather than presented as solved.
residual: Structured fields, closed filler patterns, local evidence, and this same-session review cannot authenticate reviewer identity, establish intellectual independence, prove arbitrary prose truth, prove oracle sufficiency, hash every resolved dependency artifact, prevent a concurrently running older launcher from rewriting the shared Conda prefix, supply undeclared project dependencies, or establish behavior beyond one application repository or one independently developed component repository. The authorized python-doctrine-test exercise observed conservative migration and expected authorship debt; it is not a certification of that adopter. Later bytes, field evidence, composition evidence, and independent review may refute this judgment.
